answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making trust costly to duplicate. Every newcomer stakes collateral, performs unpredictable work, and gathers attestations from reviewers outside its cluster. A mirror of signed history shows whether behavior matches claims, a fable of verified contributions replaces unbacked reputation stories, and an anchor of staked value keeps each identity accountable. Audits slash fabricated records, so spawning many identities adds expense without adding influence.
